newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech shares mixed, CEZ off despite positive result.
newsitem.headline: Czech shares mixed, CEZ off despite positive result.

text.p: Czech shares were mixed on the Prague Stock Exchnage on Friday, with minor losses to several blue chips pulling the PX50 index down 0.1 point to 558.2.
Overall, 186 issues rose on the day, while 197 fell and 157 held steady. Trading was moderate with a total of 687,004 shares changing hands on turnover of 789.7 million crowns.
SPT Telecom was the largest net decliner out of major shares, losing 20 crowns to close at 3,450.
But the market focused its attention mainly on electricity generator CEZ, on Friday, which released stronger than expected 1996 profit figures.
CEZ said its 1996 net profit, calculated according to international accounting standards (IAS), was 9.71 billion crowns, up from a previous 9.31 billion.
However, CEZ's net profit, according to Czech accounting standards, fell to 7.85 billion crowns for 1996 from 8.06 billion.
Analysts said they were pleased by the figures and dividend announcement, though CEZ shares failed to respond to the data, closing down five crowns at 1,055.
"Based on IAS figures, the results were better than I expected...I expected about nine billion crowns so its slightly higher.," said Miroslav Nosal, an equities analyst at Patria Finance.
"I expect the shares will respond favourably to the results and the fact that CEZ said dividends will be suggested to the shareholders at the AGM," he added.
CEZ has yet to pay a dividend since it was established in 1992. CEZ officials did not specify what the proposed dividend would be.

On the broader market, petrochemical firms Kaucuk and Chemopetrol both fared well, rising 70 crowns and 40 crowns respectively, after AGMs at both companies approved a merger of non-refining operations into the recently created Unipetrol a.s..

Under terms of the merger, each Kaucuk share with a nominal value of 1,000 crowns will be swapped for 12 100 crown nominally-valued shares of Unipetrol, while a 1,000 crown Chemopetrol share will be exchanged into 11 shares Unipetrol shares.
Unipetrol shares are still 100 percent held by the Czech government until the merger is complete.
Unipetrol controls fuels distribution company Benzina, as well as the 51 percent of the refining company Ceska Rafinerska, which contains the refining operations of Kaucuk and Chemopetrol.
A consortium of Conoco, Agip SpA, and Royal Dutch/Shell took the remaining 49 percent stake in Rafinerska in 1995.
